transcription: Fin Matter is a personal AI finance assistant I am building only for myself. Not a product, not for every— anyone else. Just a place where I can ask anything about my own money and get a real answer. Think of it as a chat box with total context on my finances, my credit cards, and what I actually earn in my rewards. My bank accounts, my loans and EMIs, my investments, my salary structure, how much appraisal I got, my investments across mutual funds, stock market, international stock market, any RSUs or ESOPs I have, also the NPS and EPF if there's any. And because it can see all of that All of that is a knowledge base for the chat assistant. I can ask it the questions I actually care about. Can I afford a 30 lakh car right now? If I want to buy a 5 crore retirement home for my parents, how should I plan for it? Should I spend 10 or 12 lakhs on a supercomputer to run my own AI setup? How much HRA should I show to get the maximum tax advantage? Should I be buying a ₹100 Red Bull? And yeah, the whole point is that its knowledge is my financial data and nothing else. It never invents a number. It never guesses a card benefit. Never makes up advice. All the actual money math is deterministic and provable. The AI only explains it, reasons over it, and talks to me about it. I've tried building this twice before as a full product and stalled both times because I kept trying to build the entire financial foundation before I could even ask a single question. This time, let's flip it. I want to flip it. Start with the assistant and one real question. Wire it to the real data that the question needs to answer and grow from there, expand from there. So what I want to figure out is what's the smallest version of this that's genuinely useful to me on day one? What's the one question I most want answered first? Now, how do I get my real financial data in? Do I type it in? Do I upload it manually? Do I parse it manually? Or do I automate it through email, SMS? Or do I get onboarded to account aggregators the same way other fintech apps does?

risks: Founder relapses into building the full financial foundation before shipping a single answer, repeating the two prior stalled attempts.
Manual data entry becomes a bottleneck if no lightweight ingestion path is chosen quickly for subsequent questions.
Deterministic engine (tax rules, EMI/SIP formulas, RSU vesting logic) balloons in scope if not strictly limited to the first question's needs.
Financial data goes stale without any refresh mechanism, undermining the 'never guesses' guarantee over time.
prd.problem: The founder's financial life is scattered across bank accounts, loans/EMIs, salary structure, credit cards, mutual funds, domestic and international stocks, RSUs/ESOPs, EPF and NPS, and answering a real decision like 'can I afford a 30 lakh car' or 'how should I optimize HRA' currently means manually piecing together spreadsheets and mental math with no single source of truth. Existing tools force a painful tradeoff: Finwiser and similar Account Aggregator products demand 30+ account connections before delivering any insight, FinFolio and other trackers are dashboard-first and require ongoing manual upkeep, and chat-based agents like FinNexa, Arth, and JN-66 either lose context between sessions, ignore credit card rewards and RSU/salary nuance, or aren't wired to real personal data at all. The founder has already stalled twice trying to build the full financial foundation before asking a single question — the gap in every competitor is that none let you start with one real question and grow the data model only as far as that question requires, while guaranteeing every number is deterministic and never invented by the LLM.

must_have.title: Deterministic Financial Compute Layer
must_have.rationale: Table-stakes across FinSense AI and JN-66's grounded-answer approach, and an explicit founder mandate that numbers are never invented.
must_have.description: All financial math — EMI, tax, SIP, affordability, net worth — runs through provable calculator functions; the LLM only explains results, never computes them.

must_have.title: Single-Thread Chat Interface Over Personal Knowledge Base
must_have.rationale: Table stakes established by every competitor (Finwiser, FinNexa, Arth, JN-66) as the baseline UX pattern.
must_have.description: One conversational thread where the user can ask any question about their own finances and get an answer grounded in their wired-up data.

must_have.title: First-Question Data Wiring
must_have.rationale: Directly grounded in transcript: founder stalled twice trying to build the entire foundation first and wants to flip that order.
must_have.description: Ingest only the specific data needed to answer the founder's single most important starter question, rather than building the full financial foundation upfront.

must_have.title: Core India Financial Data Model
must_have.rationale: Table stakes per competitor analysis — coverage of core India financial instruments is required for the assistant to be viable at all.
must_have.description: Structured schema covering bank accounts, loans/EMIs, salary structure, mutual funds, domestic and international stocks, RSUs/ESOPs, EPF and NPS.

must_have.title: Manual Data Entry for MVP
must_have.rationale: Table stakes ingestion requirement that directly resolves the transcript's own open question — manual entry is the fastest path to a working assistant.
must_have.description: User types or pastes real financial figures directly into the system as the initial ingestion method; no parsing or integrations required at launch.

must_have.title: Private Local Data Storage
must_have.rationale: Table stakes privacy expectation shared by FinFolio's and JN-66's local-first architectures.
must_have.description: All financial data and conversation history stored locally/privately with no third-party sharing, since this is a single-user personal tool.

wont_have.title: Mobile apps
wont_have.rationale: Explicit scope cut to hit the 72-hour window; not required to answer the first real question.
wont_have.description: No iOS/Android app; web or CLI/chat interface only for the MVP.

wont_have.title: Voice/persona customisation
wont_have.rationale: Adds interaction-layer complexity irrelevant to a single-user deterministic finance tool.
wont_have.description: No voice interface or configurable assistant personas/tone settings.

wont_have.title: Advanced integrations
wont_have.rationale: Founder explicitly wants to avoid building the full financial foundation before asking one question.
wont_have.description: No direct bank/broker API integrations, UPI sync, or Account Aggregator onboarding at launch.

wont_have.title: White-labelling
wont_have.rationale: Irrelevant for a single-user personal tool that is explicitly not a commercial product.
wont_have.description: No theming, branding, or multi-tenant configuration options.

wont_have.title: Multi-language support
wont_have.rationale: Founder is the sole user, so single-language support is sufficient for personal use.
wont_have.description: English only; no localization or regional language support.

wont_have.title: Admin dashboards
wont_have.rationale: A single-user tool has no other users or admins to manage.
wont_have.description: No admin panel, user management, or analytics dashboard.

wont_have.title: Full account aggregator onboarding
wont_have.rationale: Explicitly the pattern the founder wants to avoid based on two prior stalled attempts.
wont_have.description: No mandatory upfront connection of 30+ accounts like Finwiser before the assistant becomes useful.

wont_have.title: Multi-user support
wont_have.rationale: Transcript explicitly states this is not a product and is only for personal use.
wont_have.description: No accounts, authentication, or support for anyone other than the founder.

could_have.title: Credit Card Rewards Reasoning
could_have.rationale: Identified as a whitespace differentiation opportunity — no competitor covers credit card rewards reasoning.
could_have.description: Assistant evaluates which card to use for a purchase based on actual reward/cashback terms and current spend patterns.

could_have.title: Salary & Appraisal-Aware Tax Optimization
could_have.rationale: Differentiation opportunity: no competitor addresses salary-structure-aware tax optimization.
could_have.description: Uses actual salary structure and appraisal history to recommend optimal HRA declaration and other tax-saving choices.

could_have.title: Unified RSU/ESOP and International Stock Reasoning
could_have.rationale: Only FinFolio partially tracks RSU/ESOP and none integrate it into deterministic chat-based planning — clear whitespace.
could_have.description: Combine domestic assets with RSUs, ESOPs, and international stock holdings in one deterministic net-worth and planning engine.

could_have.title: Per-Question Ingestion Channel Selection
could_have.rationale: Differentiation opportunity: flexible, question-driven ingestion versus competitors' one-size-fits-all aggregation strategy.
could_have.description: Choose the lightest ingestion method — manual, email/SMS parsing, or Account Aggregator — per question rather than committing to one channel for everything.

should_have.title: Personalized Calculators Wired to Real Data
should_have.rationale: FinSense AI's calculators are deterministic but generic and disconnected from a real ledger — we do better by wiring them to actual personal data.
should_have.description: EMI/SIP/tax calculators like FinSense AI's, but computed against the user's actual loan, salary, and investment figures instead of generic manual inputs.

should_have.title: Persistent Financial Memory Across Sessions
should_have.rationale: FinNexa holds no data beyond a session, forcing context to be re-explained every time — persistence is a direct improvement.
should_have.description: Retain the user's financial knowledge base between conversations so context never has to be rebuilt, unlike FinNexa's session-only design.

should_have.title: Incremental Ingestion Instead of Full Aggregation Upfront
should_have.rationale: Finwiser requires 30+ account connections before delivering any insight — we invert that order to reach usefulness faster.
should_have.description: Add new data sources (email parsing, statement upload, Account Aggregator) one at a time as new questions require them, rather than connecting everything first.

should_have.title: Unified Net-Worth View Inline in Chat
should_have.rationale: FinFolio's breadth is locked behind a dashboard-first UI; delivering the same data conversationally is a lighter-weight alternative.
should_have.description: Surface relevant balances and holdings conversationally as part of an answer, instead of requiring a separate dashboard like FinFolio.

nonGoals: Not a multi-user or public product — built and used by one person only.
Not a full account-aggregation platform — no upfront connection of all financial accounts.
Not an investment advisory or execution tool — no trades, transfers, or commissioned recommendations.
Not a dashboard/visualization product — conversational chat is the only interface.
Not scoped to cover every financial data domain at launch — only what the first question requires.
prd.oneLiner: A private, deterministic AI chat assistant over one person's real financial life — built one real question at a time, not aggregated all at once like every India fintech AI project.
prd.targetUser: The founder themself — a single individual with a complex financial life (salary with appraisals, RSUs/ESOPs, credit cards, loans, EPF/NPS, domestic and international investments) who needs a private reasoning tool for real money decisions, explicitly not a mass-market product.
openQuestions: What is the single first question to wire and answer on day one — car affordability, retirement home planning, or the supercomputer purchase?
Should the first data domain be entered manually, parsed from statements, or connected via Account Aggregator?
How will credit card reward rules be sourced and kept accurate without manual upkeep?
What triggers wiring a new data domain — is it purely 'the next question I want to ask'?

successMetrics.target: First real financial question answered end-to-end within 72 hours of project start.
100% of financial calculations match manual verification across the first 20 queries within 30 days.
≥5 real financial questions asked per week by day 30 post-launch.
At least 3 financial data domains (bank, loans, investments) wired into the knowledge base within 14 days of launch.
Average self-rated CSAT of ≥4.0 out of 5 across the first 20 chat sessions within 30 days.

competitiveLandscape.positioningDelta: Requires 30+ account aggregator connections before any value; we deliver a real answer within 72 hours using only the data one question needs.
Dashboard-first asset tracker; we are chat-first and skip the dashboard entirely, wiring only what's needed.
Manual onboarding covers profile/cashflow only; we add credit card rewards, RSU/ESOP, and salary-structure tax reasoning it lacks.
Focused on spending/transactions; we extend deterministic reasoning to investments, big-purchase affordability, and tax optimization.
Session-only, no persistent memory; we retain financial context across every conversation.
Broad feature surface (UPI sync, projections, synthetic data) risks the 'build everything first' trap; we intentionally stay narrow and incremental.
Generic calculators not tied to real personal accounts; ours are wired directly to the user's actual salary, loans, and investments.

# FinNexa 💰

**FinNexa** is an AI-powered personal finance assistant that helps users *talk to their money*. 
It connects securely to the **Fi Money MCP (Model Context Protocol)** to analyze real financial data and explain it in simple, human language.

The goal of FinNexa is **financial literacy** — helping people understand where their money goes, how healthy their finances are, and what they can do better.

---

## 🚀 What Problem Does FinNexa Solve?

Most people have access to financial data, but:
- It’s scattered across banks, mutual funds, EPF, credit cards
- Dashboards are complex and intimidating
- Insights are numbers, not explanations

**FinNexa converts raw financial data into meaningful conversations.**

Instead of charts and jargon, users can ask:
- “Where am I overspending?”
- “How healthy are my finances?”
- “What should I improve next month?”
- “Why is my net worth going up or down?”

---

1. **Fi Money MCP** provides verified financial data (read-only)

3. An AI model analyzes only that data

- AI is strictly restricted to provided data only

competitors.marketSummary: There's a small but active wave of India-focused open-source/hobbyist 'AI + personal finance' projects (hackathon builds, self-hosted trackers, and one funded-looking RIA startup) all converging on the same insight: users want a single conversational interface over their fragmented financial data (banks, investments, EPF/NPS, loans, RSUs) instead of dashboards. Most projects solve either (a) broad automated data aggregation (Finwiser, FinFolio) or (b) a chat/agent layer with deterministic math (FinSense AI, JN-66, Arth), but none combine deep personal breadth (credit card rewards, RSU/ESOP, salary/appraisal, international stocks, NPS/EPF) with a strictly deterministic, provable-math chat assistant built incrementally around single real questions rather than full-platform ingestion upfront. This confirms the space is real and validated, but fragmented and mostly unfinished/hobby-grade — no one has nailed the 'start with one question, wire only what's needed' incremental build philosophy.
competitors.ourPositioning: Fin Matter is not a product competing for users but a deliberately narrow, deterministic personal finance chat assistant built for one person's real financial life — including credit card rewards, RSUs, salary/appraisal, and NPS/EPF — where every number is provably sourced from real data and the system grows one real question at a time instead of demanding full financial aggregation upfront like every existing India fintech AI project.

Salary structure and appraisal-aware tax optimization (e.g., optimal HRA declaration) — unaddressed by all

Strict separation of deterministic financial computation layer from LLM reasoning/explanation layer as an explicit architectural guarantee (most competitors let the LLM touch numbers directly)
Radically incremental 'one question, wire only needed data' build philosophy vs. every competitor's 'aggregate everything first' approach — reduces time-to-value dramatically

Single-user, not-a-product mindset removing scalability/onboarding-flow overhead that burdens Finwiser/FinFolio, allowing faster iteration on real personal edge cases (₹100 Red Bull-level judgment calls)

hld.dataFlow: User submits a question in Chat UI → Chat Orchestrator sends message + conversation history + tool schema to LLM → LLM returns a tool call (e.g. compute_affordability, get_net_worth) → Orchestrator validates inputs against Financial Data Store and executes the matching Deterministic Compute Engine function → Result + calculation trace is written to Calculation Audit Log → Orchestrator sends the structured numeric result back to the LLM Explanation Service with an instruction to explain-only-do-not-compute → LLM returns natural language explanation → Orchestrator persists both the user message and assistant response (with trace) in Conversation Memory Store → Chat UI renders the answer. New financial domains are only added to the Financial Data Store, via manual entry forms, when a new question requires them.
hld.overview: Fin Matter is a single-user, privacy-first financial reasoning assistant. It pairs a conversational chat interface with a strictly deterministic financial compute layer: the LLM is only ever permitted to explain numbers that were produced by verified calculator functions running against the user's own structured financial data in Postgres. The data model grows incrementally — only the tables needed to answer the current question are populated via manual entry — rather than requiring full account aggregation upfront. Every chat turn is logged with the underlying calculation trace so results can be manually verified for accuracy.

components.name: Chat UI
components.responsibility: Single-thread Next.js web interface where the user types financial questions and reads grounded answers; also hosts manual data-entry forms for each financial domain (bank, loans, salary, cards, investments, RSU/ESOP, EPF/NPS).

components.name: Chat Orchestrator (API layer)
components.responsibility: Receives user messages, calls the LLM with tool/function definitions describing available deterministic calculators and data queries, executes the tools the LLM selects, and re-invokes the LLM only to phrase an explanation of the returned numeric results.

components.name: Deterministic Financial Compute Engine
components.responsibility: Pure, unit-tested TypeScript functions for EMI, SIP, tax (old/new regime), affordability, RSU vesting value, net worth aggregation, and credit-card reward math. No LLM involvement; every function is independently verifiable.

components.name: LLM Explanation Service
components.responsibility: Wraps an LLM (function-calling capable) that (a) maps natural language to the correct calculator/query tool call and (b) turns structured numeric results into a plain-English answer — never invents figures itself.

components.name: Financial Data Store
components.responsibility: Supabase Postgres schema holding the user's real financial entities (bank accounts, loans, salary structure, credit cards, mutual funds, domestic/international stocks, RSU/ESOP grants, EPF, NPS) — populated incrementally via manual entry.

components.name: Conversation Memory Store
components.responsibility: Persists chat threads and messages, including the calculation trace attached to each assistant response, so context and prior answers survive across sessions.

components.name: Auth Service
components.responsibility: Supabase Auth restricting the app to a single authenticated user (the founder); protects all data and chat endpoints via row-level security.

components.name: Calculation Audit Log
components.responsibility: Stores every calculator invocation (inputs, outputs, function version) tied to the chat message that triggered it, enabling manual accuracy verification against the success metric.

engineering.schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  email text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  display_name text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE bank_accounts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  bank_name text NOT NULL,
  account_type text NOT NULL,
  balance numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  as_of_date date NOT NULL DEFAULT current_date,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE loans (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  loan_type text NOT NULL,
  principal numeric NOT NULL,
  interest_rate_pct numeric NOT NULL,
  tenure_months integer NOT NULL,
  start_date date NOT NULL,
  outstanding_balance numeric NOT NULL,
  emi_amount numeric,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE salary_structures (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  effective_date date NOT NULL,
  basic numeric NOT NULL,
  hra numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  special_allowance numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  bonus_annual numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  employer_pf_contribution numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  tax_regime text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE credit_cards (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  card_name text NOT NULL,
  credit_limit numeric NOT NULL,
  current_outstanding numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  reward_rules jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE mutual_fund_holdings (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  fund_name text NOT NULL,
  units numeric NOT NULL,
  avg_nav numeric NOT NULL,
  current_nav numeric,
  sip_amount numeric,
  as_of_date date NOT NULL DEFAULT current_date,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE stock_holdings (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ticker text NOT NULL,
  market text NOT NULL,
  quantity numeric NOT NULL,
  avg_price numeric NOT NULL,
  current_price numeric,
  currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INR',
  as_of_date date NOT NULL DEFAULT current_date,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE rsu_grants (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  grant_type text NOT NULL,
  company text NOT NULL,
  total_units numeric NOT NULL,
  vested_units numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  grant_date date NOT NULL,
  vesting_schedule jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  strike_price numeric,
  current_price numeric,
  currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE epf_accounts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  current_balance numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  employee_monthly_contribution numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  employer_monthly_contribution numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  as_of_date date NOT NULL DEFAULT current_date,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE nps_accounts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  current_balance numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  monthly_contribution numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  asset_allocation jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  as_of_date date NOT NULL DEFAULT current_date,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE conversation_threads (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE calculation_logs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  function_name text NOT NULL,
  function_version text NOT NULL,
  inputs jsonb NOT NULL,
  outputs jsonb NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE messages (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  thread_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES conversation_threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role text NOT NULL,
  content text NOT NULL,
  calculation_log_id uuid REFERENCES calculation_logs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

openEngineeringQuestions: What is the single first question to wire and answer on day one, and which minimal set of tables does it require to be populated first?
Should manual data entry be free-form (LLM-assisted parsing into structured fields) or strictly structured forms to guarantee no LLM involvement in data capture itself?
How will credit card reward rules be sourced and kept accurate over time without manual upkeep becoming a maintenance burden?
What staleness threshold on as_of_date should trigger a UI warning that a number may be out of date, to protect the 'never guesses' guarantee?
Should the deterministic compute engine be versioned per function (function_version) so historical calculation_logs remain valid if formulas change later (e.g., tax law updates)?
What is the trigger/workflow for deciding when to add a new financial domain table — purely 'the next question I want to ask', and who/what enforces that discipline against scope creep?

transcription: go. So most people walk into an architect's office with a plot size, a Pinterest board, and no idea what they actually want, and pay in months of revisions to find out. The product turns that first conversation into a working model before the appointment. You describe the plot, the road, the family, and how you live. If you are into Vastu, uh, If you are into Vastu, you share your, uh, preferences. You share the direction of your plot, the facing of your plot, and, uh, in plain language, all of it in plain language. It asks the questions an architect, a senior architect, would ask you. Which way does it face? Who sleeps where? How many cars do you want? Do you follow Vastu or not? Then it draws you floor plans. You can argue with. You can actually come back any number of times you want for those floor plans. And then it builds the house as a 3D model you can spin like a dollhouse, lift floor by floor, and walk through at eye height from the gate to the roof. Change your mind about the kitchen and the model changes with you. What you take to the architect is not a blank slate. But a plan you have stood inside, you have roamed inside, you have checked every inch of it inside, with the reasons for each design written down so the professional's time goes into making it buildable rather than guessing what you actually want. Why it works and what it doesn't— the value is in the reasoning layer, not the renderer. Room sizes that are honest about the plot, parking that respects the road, Orientation and Vastu placements, the trade-offs said out loud. So yeah.

risks: Generating a full eye-height walkable 3D model (vs. just a dollhouse) may exceed what's achievable with available AI tooling inside 72 hours
Vastu, climate, and setback rule logic combined could produce unbuildable or non-compliant layouts without expert validation, undermining trust
Users may expect legally sanctioned drawings despite disclaimers, creating the same liability confusion competitors already flag
Conversational, lifestyle-driven intake is inherently more complex to build than a static form, risking scope creep within the build window
prd.problem: People walk into an architect's office with a plot size, a Pinterest board, and no real idea of what they want, then pay in months of revisions to discover it — the transcript describes this exact blind first meeting as the industry norm. Today's coping mechanism is either hiring an architect cold and iterating expensively, or using AI generators like GrehYug, Cadbull, or Naksha that take a static form (plot, facing, BHK, Vastu toggle) and spit out a one-shot plan for a flat fee, with no room to argue with it and no explanation of why any room sits where it does. Architect-catalog platforms like Architects House solve speed with presets, but you're customizing someone else's archetype, not designing from how your family actually lives. The gap the market leaves open: no tool treats the brief as a conversation about lifestyle, lets you revise for free until it's right, or hands the architect a walkable model with the reasoning already written down — so the professional's time still goes into guessing instead of building.

hld.dataFlow: User signs in → creates a Project → Conversational Intake UI collects plot/facing/family/Vastu answers, sent to Intake Orchestration Service which structures and stores them as intake_responses → on 'generate', Floor Plan Generation Engine reads intake_responses + plot data, applies Vastu & Setback Rules Engine to produce a versioned floor_plans record with nested rooms → Design Rationale Generator attaches rationale_text per room/category → 3D Model Service converts layout_json into a model asset consumed by the browser-side Three.js viewer; PDF Export Service renders the same layout_json into a PDF stored in Supabase Storage → user reviews the dollhouse model and PDF, can revise intake (creating a new floor_plan version) at no cost → once satisfied, user completes checkout (Orders) which unlocks final downloadable assets.
hld.overview: Aavaas is a web application that converts a conversational plot-and-lifestyle intake into a rule-validated floor plan, a spinnable 3D dollhouse model, a PDF export, and written design rationale. The system combines an LLM-driven conversational intake layer, a deterministic Vastu/setback rules engine, a layout generation service that produces structured room geometry, and a client-side 3D renderer that consumes that geometry. Users can iterate on the intake and regenerate plans for free, with each iteration versioned so they can compare and revert. A single checkout unlocks the final downloadable package (PDF + rationale + 3D export).

components.name: Conversational Intake UI
components.responsibility: Guides the user through plain-language questions about plot, facing, family composition, sleeping arrangements, parking, and Vastu preference; stores structured answers incrementally.

components.name: Intake Orchestration Service (LLM)
components.responsibility: Uses an LLM to turn free-text/guided answers into structured intake fields, ask clarifying follow-ups, and detect when enough information exists to generate a plan.

components.name: Floor Plan Generation Engine
components.responsibility: Combines plot geometry, BHK requirements, and intake data with the Vastu/setback rules engine to produce a structured room-by-room layout (positions, dimensions, zones).

components.name: Vastu & Setback Rules Engine
components.responsibility: Deterministic rule set (strict/light/none Vastu modes, municipal setback norms by road width) that validates and adjusts room placement produced by the generation engine.

components.name: Design Rationale Generator (LLM)
components.responsibility: Generates one-line written reasoning per major room/trade-off decision (orientation, Vastu, parking, climate) tied to the layout output.

components.name: 3D Model Service
components.responsibility: Converts the structured layout JSON into a renderable 3D scene definition (walls, floors, room volumes) consumed by a client-side Three.js/React-Three-Fiber viewer for spin/floor-lift interaction.

components.name: PDF Export Service
components.responsibility: Renders the 2D floor plan, dimensions, Vastu zones, and rationale notes into a downloadable PDF.

components.name: Revision & Versioning Service
components.responsibility: Tracks intake edits and regenerated floor plan versions per project, enabling free unlimited iteration and rollback.

components.name: Payments & Checkout
components.responsibility: Handles the single paid checkout that unlocks final PDF/3D export downloads.

components.name: Auth & Profile Service
components.responsibility: Manages user sign-up/login and project ownership via Supabase Auth.

components.name: Storage
components.responsibility: Stores generated PDFs, 3D model assets, and intermediate layout artifacts in Supabase Storage.

engineering.schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE profiles (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  full_name text,
  phone text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE projects (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  plot_width numeric,
  plot_length numeric,
  plot_area numeric,
  facing text,
  road_width numeric,
  vastu_preference text CHECK (vastu_preference IN ('strict','light','none')) DEFAULT 'light',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','generated','paid')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE intake_responses (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  question_key text NOT NULL,
  answer jsonb NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE floor_plans (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  bhk_count int,
  total_area numeric,
  layout_json jsonb NOT NULL,
  pdf_url text,
  is_current boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE rooms (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  floor_plan_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES floor_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  room_type text NOT NULL,
  floor_number int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  width numeric,
  length numeric,
  position_x numeric,
  position_y numeric,
  orientation text,
  vastu_zone text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE design_rationales (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  floor_plan_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES floor_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  room_id uuid REFERENCES rooms(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  category text NOT NULL CHECK (category IN ('orientation','vastu','parking','climate','family')),
  rationale_text text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE model_assets (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  floor_plan_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES floor_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  asset_type text NOT NULL CHECK (asset_type IN ('dollhouse','walkthrough')),
  file_url text NOT NULL,
  format text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'gltf',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE revisions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  floor_plan_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES floor_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  change_summary text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  amount numeric NOT NULL,
  currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INR',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','paid','failed','refunded')),
  payment_provider text,
  payment_reference text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE vastu_rules (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  room_type text NOT NULL,
  preferred_zone text NOT NULL,
  priority int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  description text
);

techStack.llm: OpenAI GPT-4o (or equivalent) used for: (1) conversational intake structuring/follow-up questions, (2) assisting layout heuristics alongside the deterministic Vastu/setback rules engine, (3) generating one-line design rationale text.
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth (email/password + OAuth) with RLS policies tying rows to auth.uid().
techStack.infra: Vercel for frontend/API hosting, Supabase Storage for PDF and 3D asset files, Supabase Postgres managed DB.
techStack.backend: Next.js API Routes / Supabase Edge Functions for orchestration (intake processing, layout generation, rationale generation, PDF rendering, checkout webhooks).
techStack.database: Supabase Postgres with Row Level Security scoped per user_id/project_id.
techStack.devtools: TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Zod for schema validation, GitHub Actions for CI (lint/typecheck/test), Vercel Preview Deployments.
techStack.frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router) + React + TypeScript + TailwindCSS; React-Three-Fiber/Three.js for the spinnable 3D dollhouse viewer; React Hook Form + Zod for the conversational intake steps.

transcription: VibeGraph is a creative generation platform for founders and startup teams. Think of it as one place to build and fetch everything you need from a creative and brand point of view. You give it some input about your startup or project, what it does, who is it for, the vibe you are going for. And it produces your entire brand and creative foundation from that. Your full brand identity, logo, color palette, typography, and the whole visual system. Then the artifacts you actually run a company with. Your design system for your product, landing pages design, campaign creatives, social graphics, illustrations, even animations, and the UI/UX for your entire product. And for teams that build a real frontend design system— components, tokens, spacing, scales— not just pretty pictures. There's an LLM at the core orchestrating all of it, making the brand decisions and driving the generations so everything stays coherent. Across every asset. Its identity as a service, but broader— the single creative layer a startup plugs into from first logo to full campaign. The feel we want for Vibe Graph's own brand is modern, confident, and creative without being childish or gimmicky. A serious tool for people who care about design, not at all. Once the application, once the product has formed a context around your startup or your idea, whenever you come to the platform, you just ask for what you need. You need an ad campaign for some of your feature, you want a social media post for your XYZ feature, you will get You'll get artifacts for that. Vibe graph need to be premium, sharp, a little bold, something that signals taste.

prd.problem: Founders and small startup teams need a coherent brand and creative foundation fast, but today they either hire expensive designers, cobble together Canva templates and one-off logo generators, or bounce between disconnected tools — a brand-kit generator for the logo, a Figma plugin for imagery, a social tool for posts — and end up with a brand that looks different on every surface. Existing 'vibe-to-brand' tools like VibeKit stop at a static identity kit with no path to product UI or ongoing assets; general creative canvases like VibePaper have no persistent brand memory; and the closest full-stack competitor, run:VibesAI, is enterprise-leaning, early-stage, and doesn't go deep on frontend design systems (tokens, components, spacing). The gap is a premium, opinionated platform that forms real brand context once and then produces everything from logo to landing page to product UI/UX to campaign creative on demand, coherently.

must_have.title: Founder Brief Intake
must_have.rationale: Table stakes — fast onboarding via conversational/form input is required across all competitors.
must_have.description: Structured conversational input capturing what the startup does, who it's for, and the desired vibe.

must_have.title: Core Brand Identity Generation
must_have.rationale: Table stakes — every competitor delivers logo/color/typography as the baseline deliverable.
must_have.description: Generates logo, color palette, and typography system from the intake brief.

must_have.title: Persistent Brand Context Memory
must_have.rationale: Table stakes — brand context memory to keep outputs consistent is identified as non-viable to skip.
must_have.description: The platform retains the generated brand foundation so future requests stay visually and tonally consistent.

must_have.title: On-Brand Asset Generation
must_have.rationale: Table stakes — ability to generate on-brand social/marketing graphics is required to be viable.
must_have.description: Generate marketing/social graphics and campaign creatives that automatically apply the stored brand system.

must_have.title: Asset Export
must_have.rationale: Table stakes — exportable assets are listed as required across the competitive set.
must_have.description: Download generated logos, graphics, and design files in standard formats for external use.

wont_have.title: Mobile Apps
wont_have.rationale: Explicit scope cut to protect the 72-hour build window.
wont_have.description: No native iOS/Android app in the MVP; web-only access.

wont_have.title: Voice/Persona Customisation
wont_have.rationale: Not part of founder's stated MVP scope; adds conversational-UX complexity we're not competing on.
wont_have.description: No customizable AI assistant persona or voice tone selection beyond the default brand director.

wont_have.title: Advanced Integrations
wont_have.rationale: run:VibesAI and VibeFlow compete on integrations/publishing pipelines; we punt this to focus on core generation quality.
wont_have.description: No Figma sync, CMS publishing, or CRM/marketing-tool integrations at launch.

wont_have.title: White-Labelling
wont_have.rationale: Out of scope for a single-startup-facing MVP shipped in 72 hours.
wont_have.description: No ability for agencies or resellers to rebrand VibeGraph as their own product.

wont_have.title: Multi-Language Support
wont_have.rationale: Localization adds generation and QA overhead not justified for an MVP validation window.
wont_have.description: Platform and generated copy ship in English only.

wont_have.title: Admin Dashboards
wont_have.rationale: Not needed to validate core value prop for a solo founder in the MVP timeframe.
wont_have.description: No team-management, permissions, or usage-analytics dashboard.

wont_have.title: Real-Time Team Collaboration Canvas
wont_have.rationale: We are explicitly not competing on general-purpose collaborative canvas tooling.
wont_have.description: No live multi-user editing canvas like VibePaper's shared workspace.

wont_have.title: Direct Social Auto-Publishing
wont_have.rationale: VibeFlow owns this wedge; we generate assets but don't compete on publishing automation for the MVP.
wont_have.description: No automated posting to LinkedIn/X or other channels.

could_have.title: Frontend Design System Output
could_have.rationale: Differentiation opportunity — no competitor offers production-grade frontend design system depth.
could_have.description: Generate design tokens, components, spacing, and scale for teams that need a real frontend system, not just images.

could_have.title: Product UI/UX Generation
could_have.rationale: Differentiation opportunity — full product UI/UX generation is a gap every competitor leaves open.
could_have.description: Generate screens and flows for a startup's actual product tied to the same brand system.

could_have.title: Unified Creative Request Hub
could_have.rationale: Differentiation opportunity — replacing the need to stitch together multiple point solutions is unaddressed by competitors.
could_have.description: Single place to request any artifact type instead of stitching together separate brand, design, and social tools.

should_have.title: LLM Creative Director Orchestration
should_have.rationale: run:VibesAI syncs a source-of-truth but lacks a decision-making creative layer; we can out-orchestrate them with LLM-driven judgment.
should_have.description: A central LLM makes brand decisions and drives every generation so outputs stay coherent across asset types, better than run:VibesAI's more mechanical token-sync approach.

should_have.title: On-Demand Ask-For-What-You-Need Generation
should_have.rationale: VibeKit stops at initial brand identity; we extend the same context indefinitely per the founder's stated 'ask for what you need' vision.
should_have.description: After setup, users just request an artifact (an ad, a social post, a feature graphic) and get it instantly, unlike VibeKit's one-time brand kit delivery.

should_have.title: Premium Sharp Aesthetic Direction
should_have.rationale: Competitor analysis flags VibeKit as playful and run:VibesAI as generic enterprise — we can win on taste-driven premium positioning.
should_have.description: Default output style is confident and bold rather than playful, differentiating tone from VibeKit's indie-fun voice and run:VibesAI's generic enterprise tone.

prd.oneLiner: The single LLM-orchestrated creative layer that takes a startup from first logo to full product design system and ongoing campaign creative — where VibeKit stops at a brand kit and run:VibesAI stays enterprise and shallow on frontend design systems.
prd.targetUser: Solo founders and small startup teams (pre-seed to Series A) who need to look and build like a funded, design-serious company without hiring a design team.
openQuestions: What is the pricing model — one-time brand kit fee, subscription, or usage-based credits for ongoing asset requests?
How many revision rounds are included before an asset generation counts as 'delivered' for CSAT measurement?
What's the minimum viable set of product UI/UX screens needed to prove the frontend design system claim without over-building for 72 hours?
Should the MVP support team accounts (multiple founders per startup) or strictly single-user in v1?

# vibe-aigc

Implementation of the Vibe AIGC paper ([arXiv:2602.04575](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04575)). Decomposes high-level creative intent ("Vibes") into executable multi-step content generation workflows via agentic orchestration.

## What it does

You describe what you want (a "Vibe" -- style, constraints, description). A MetaPlanner breaks it into a DAG of tasks, assigns tools, executes nodes (with parallelism where possible), and returns composed output. If a node fails, it replans.

```python
from vibe_aigc import Vibe, MetaPlanner

vibe = Vibe(
    description="Write a blog post about AI agents",
    style="informative, engaging",
    constraints=["under 1000 words"]
)

planner = MetaPlanner()
result = await planner.execute(vibe)
```

## Architecture

Based on the paper's 3-component design:

| Component | Role | Module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MetaPlanner | Decomposes Vibes into workflow DAGs | `vibe_aigc.planner` |
| KnowledgeBase | Domain expertise (film, writing, design, music) | `vibe_aigc.knowledge` |
| ToolRegistry | Atomic content generation tools | `vibe_aigc.tools` |

Additional modules handle ComfyUI workflow composition, video/audio pipelines, VLM feedback loops, and multi-GPU execution.

## LLM backends

| Provider | Config | Key required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var | Yes |
| Anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var | Yes |
| Ollama | `LLMConfig.for_ollama(host=..., model=...)` | No |

CREATE TABLE profiles (

  email text NOT NULL,
  full_name text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE brands (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
  vibe_summary text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE founder_briefs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES brands(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  what_it_does text NOT NULL,
  target_audience text NOT NULL,
  desired_vibe text NOT NULL,
  raw_answers jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE brand_assets (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES brands(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  asset_type text NOT NULL,
  file_url text,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE design_tokens (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES brands(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_category text NOT NULL,
  token_key text NOT NULL,
  token_value text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE asset_requests (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  brand_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES brands(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  requested_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  request_type text NOT NULL,
  prompt_text text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at timestamptz
);

transcription: Poké Clash is a mobile creature battling game built around the fantasy of becoming the greatest trainer alive. You start with a single companion creature and set out on a journey, walking routes, catching wild creatures to grow your collection, and battling other trainers along the way. Every battle is a duel of stats. Each creature is scored across a handful of categories like attack, defense, speed, and special power. And in battle, you pick which category to fight on, turn by turn, whittling down your opponent's health. On top of the raw numbers sit 2 layers of depth. First, elemental types— fire, water, grass, electric, rock— that beat and lose to each other in a rock-paper-scissors triangle. So your strongest strat can be neutralized by a bad matchup, and category choice becomes a real read against your opponent. Second, unique abilities each creature carries which bend the rules of the duel— stealing a strat, forcing a category, shrugging off a type disadvantage. The world is structured as a series of gems. Each themed around a type and guarded by a leader. Beat the leader, earn a badge, and after a hard-won victory, you even get to swap one of your creatures for one of theirs. Collect all the badges, top the leaderboard, and prove you're the best. The long-term vision is online multiplayer where trainers battle each other directly. But the heart of it is a single-player story mode you can lose yourself in. In the initial phase of the project, the multi— we would go with a single-player story mode where the other trainers would be AI-powered. This is a passion project first, an idea that's been kicking around for years, and this is about finally building it. As interactive, and as fun as it can possibly be. On strategy, the plan is to prototype privately against real creature data to nail down whether the battle loop is genuinely fun, moving fast without worrying about art or originality. And only later, if the game proves worth it, invest in a set of original creatures For anything that goes public, validate the fun first, own the world second.

prd.problem: Trainer-fantasy players want the exact feeling of Pokémon-style dueling — read your opponent, pick a stat category, get punished by a bad type matchup, pull off a game-changing ability — but nothing legally original and mobile-native delivers it. Today that itch gets fed by playing decades-old console Pokémon titles, downloading shallow gesture-drawing clones like Poke Clash: Monster Hunter that ditch strategy for touch gimmicks, grinding unofficial fan-made MMO servers that lean directly on Pokémon IP at real legal risk, or settling for card-combo roguelites like Creature Clash: Echoes that trade readable stat-vs-stat duels for deck-building abstraction. The research confirms the gap: no competitor combines simple, transparent stat-category combat with a real elemental triangle AND rule-bending unique abilities AND a persistent badge-driven journey in a legally clean, mobile-first package — most competitors sacrifice one of those three to ship something safe or fast.

must_have.title: Stat-category turn duel
must_have.description: Each turn, pick attack, defense, speed, or special power to whittle down the opponent's HP; this is the core strategic loop the transcript is built around.

must_have.title: Elemental type triangle
must_have.description: Fire, water, grass, electric, and rock beat and lose to each other, forcing category choice to double as a read against the opponent's type.

must_have.title: Creature catching & collection
must_have.description: Walk routes and catch wild creatures to grow a roster; this is table-stakes across every competitor in the category.

must_have.title: Gym/badge journey structure
must_have.description: World is divided into type-themed gyms guarded by leaders; beating a leader earns a badge and unlocks the next zone, the table-stakes progression spine of the genre.

must_have.title: Creature growth/leveling
must_have.description: Creatures gain strength through battles fought along the journey, matching the growth/evolution loop every competitor offers.

must_have.title: AI-powered single-player trainers
must_have.description: All opposing trainers are AI-controlled for this initial phase, exactly as the founder scoped it before investing in real multiplayer.

wont_have.title: Native app store distribution
wont_have.description: MVP ships as a private prototype build, not a published iOS/Android app, per the founder's plan to validate fun before going public.

wont_have.title: Voice/persona customization
wont_have.description: No voice acting or trainer/creature persona customization; art and originality are explicitly deprioritized until the battle loop proves fun.

wont_have.title: Advanced integrations
wont_have.description: No social login, ad SDKs, or analytics platform integrations; unnecessary overhead for a closed private prototype.

wont_have.title: White-labelling
wont_have.description: No reskinning or licensing the engine for other IP; this is a passion-project original world, not a platform product.

wont_have.title: Multi-language support
wont_have.description: English-only for the prototype; localization is irrelevant until the core loop is validated.

wont_have.title: Admin dashboards
wont_have.description: No internal content-management or live-ops tooling; there's no daily content cadence to manage in a private single-player test.

wont_have.title: Online multiplayer PvP
wont_have.description: Real trainer-vs-trainer battling is the explicit long-term vision, deliberately deferred in favor of AI-powered single-player for this phase.

wont_have.title: Original creature art & world-building
wont_have.description: Prototype runs on real/placeholder creature data to test the battle loop; original art investment comes only after the fun is proven, per the founder's stated strategy.

could_have.title: Rule-bending unique abilities
could_have.description: Creature abilities that steal a strat, force a category, or shrug off a type disadvantage — a whitespace layer no competitor offers.

could_have.title: Post-badge creature swap reward
could_have.description: Defeating a gym leader lets you swap one of your creatures for one of theirs, deepening collection strategy beyond simple catching, an untapped differentiator.

could_have.title: Adaptive AI trainer difficulty
could_have.description: AI opponents that scale behavior to player skill, offering a more dynamic stepping stone toward real PvP than the scripted AI seen in fan-game competitors.

should_have.title: Simplified 5-element type chart
should_have.description: Use five elements instead of the official Pokémon franchise's 18-type chart, keeping strategic depth while cutting onboarding time for a mobile session.

should_have.title: No-pay-to-win economy
should_have.description: Free to play with cosmetic/convenience monetization only, matching and sharpening Creature Clash: Echoes' anti-pay-to-win stance to build trust fast.

should_have.title: Lightweight persistent leaderboard
should_have.description: A simple, always-on ranking by badges/wins, improving on Poke Clash (Bang-Bang)'s abandoned daily-drop leaderboard that requires ongoing content ops.

prd.oneLiner: The mobile creature-battler that finally makes transparent stat-category dueling and rule-bending abilities the strategic core Pokémon clones, card-abstracted roguelites, and IP-risky fan servers never built.
prd.targetUser: A solo trainer-fantasy player (and, for the MVP, the founder's own private playtest pool) who grew up on Pokémon-style dueling and wants deep, readable strategy on their phone rather than gesture gimmicks, card abstraction, or IP-risky fan servers.
openQuestions: Do we build the prototype in an existing engine (Unity) or a fast web build to hit the 72-hour window?
How many creatures and abilities are the minimum needed to genuinely test the rock-paper-scissors + ability-bending interaction?
Who are the 15 private playtesters and how are they recruited within the timeline?
What placeholder creature data source do we use to avoid IP risk during private validation?
What threshold on the strategic-swing and CSAT metrics triggers the decision to invest in original art and world-building?

successMetrics.metric: Battle completion rate among private playtesters
successMetrics.target: ≥80% of started test battles completed without abandonment within the first 2 weeks of prototype testing
≥60% of the 15-tester private pool play 3+ sessions within the first 30 days

successMetrics.metric: CSAT on battle-loop fun (1-5 scale survey)
successMetrics.target: average CSAT ≥4.0/5 across at least 15 testers by day 30

successMetrics.metric: Strategic-swing rate (battles decided by type/ability read, not raw stats)
successMetrics.target: ≥30% of the first 100 recorded test battles show a type or ability-driven reversal

competitors.marketSummary: The creature-battling genre is dominated by the untouchable Pokémon franchise, with a long tail of low-quality mobile clones (Poke Clash variants), unofficial fan projects trading on the IP directly, and one modern, well-produced indie contender (Creature Clash: Echoes) that has successfully translated the formula into a mobile-native, story-driven experience. No competitor combines simple, readable stat-category dueling with a type triangle AND unique rule-bending abilities AND a persistent open-world journey/badge structure in a legally original, mobile-first package — most either sacrifice strategic depth for casual/arcade mechanics, abstract combat into cards, or risk IP infringement by leaning on Pokémon assets outright.
competitors.ourPositioning: Poké Clash aims to be the mobile creature-battler that finally nails the strategic heart of Pokémon-style dueling — transparent stat-category combat layered with type triangles and rule-bending abilities — in an original, legally sound package, differentiating from shallow arcade clones, IP-risky fan projects, and card-abstracted roguelites like Creature Clash: Echoes. We win by validating a genuinely fun, mind-game-rich battle loop first, then investing in world and creature identity second.
differentiationOpportunities: Simple, transparent stat-category dueling (pick attack/defense/speed/special) as the core turn mechanic — more readable and mind-game-driven than card combos or gesture drawing
Unique creature abilities that actively bend battle rules (stealing strats, forcing categories, ignoring type disadvantage) — no competitor offers this rule-bending layer
Post-boss-battle creature swap with gym leaders as a signature reward mechanic, deepening collection strategy beyond simple catching
AI-powered trainers in single-player mode as a stepping stone to genuine online PvP, offering more dynamic/adaptive opponents than scripted fan-game AI
Original, legally-clean IP validated via private prototyping — avoids the legal risk seen in fan-made 'Poke Clash'/itch.io clones
Focus on 'fun-first, art-second' lean validation, enabling rapid iteration on the battle loop that bloated MMO fangames and shallow arcade clones lack

hld.dataFlow: Player authenticates via Supabase Auth → Next.js client fetches roster/gym state from Postgres via API routes → player enters a battle screen where each turn the client posts a stat-category choice to the Battle Engine → Battle Engine loads both trainers' active creatures, applies type-triangle multipliers and ability rules, computes damage, and returns the turn result → result and any strategic-swing flag are persisted to battles/battle_turns/battle_events → on battle end, creature XP/level, badge unlock, and leaderboard rows are updated → client polls or subscribes (Supabase Realtime) to reflect updated roster, badges, and leaderboard standings.
hld.overview: Poké Clash MVP is a mobile-responsive web prototype (installable via browser, no app store distribution) built on Next.js and Supabase. It delivers a single-player, AI-driven creature-battling loop centered on transparent stat-category duels, a 5-element type triangle, creature catching, leveling, and a gym/badge progression spine. The architecture is intentionally lean for a 15-person private playtest: a monolithic Next.js app handles UI, battle logic, and API routes; Supabase provides auth, Postgres data storage, and realtime sync for leaderboard updates; an in-process battle engine (server-side) resolves turns deterministically so results can be audited for the strategic-swing metric. No native app, no multiplayer networking, no CMS/admin tooling — everything is scoped to validate whether the battle loop is fun.

components.name: Next.js Web Client
components.responsibility: Mobile-responsive UI for catching, roster management, gym navigation, and turn-based battle screen; communicates with backend via API routes.

components.name: Battle Engine (Server-side module)
components.responsibility: Deterministic resolution of stat-category picks, type-triangle multipliers, and rule-bending ability effects; produces per-turn logs for analytics.

components.name: AI Trainer Controller
components.responsibility: Selects stat-category/move choices for opponent trainers using simple heuristics (with a scoped hook for future adaptive difficulty).

components.name: Supabase Auth
components.responsibility: Email/password login restricted to the private playtester allowlist; issues session tokens consumed by Next.js middleware.

components.name: Supabase Postgres
components.responsibility: Stores users, creatures, species/type/ability reference data, gyms/badges, battles, and leaderboard aggregates.

components.name: Leaderboard Service
components.responsibility: Recomputes and serves badge/win rankings on battle completion; lightweight, no scheduled jobs needed given player volume.

components.name: Analytics/Metrics Logger
components.responsibility: Records battle completion, session counts, and strategic-swing flags (type/ability-driven reversals) into a battle_events table for success-metric reporting.

components.name: Vercel Hosting/CI
components.responsibility: Builds and deploys the Next.js app, manages environment secrets, and serves the prototype to the 15-tester pool.

engineering.schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  display_name text,
  created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE species (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name text NOT NULL,
  element_type text NOT NULL CHECK (element_type IN ('fire','water','grass','electric','rock')),
  base_attack int NOT NULL,
  base_defense int NOT NULL,
  base_speed int NOT NULL,
  base_special int NOT NULL,
  base_hp int NOT NULL,
  catch_rate numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5
);

CREATE TABLE abilities (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name text NOT NULL,
  effect_type text NOT NULL CHECK (effect_type IN ('steal_strat','force_category','ignore_type_disadvantage','other')),
  effect_config jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);

CREATE TABLE species_abilities (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  species_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES species(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ability_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES abilities(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE creature_instances (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  owner_id uuid REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  species_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES species(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  nickname text,
  level int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  xp int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  current_hp int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  is_active_roster boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  caught_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE gyms (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name text NOT NULL,
  element_type text NOT NULL CHECK (element_type IN ('fire','water','grass','electric','rock')),
  leader_species_id uuid REFERENCES species(id),
  order_index int NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE badges (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  gym_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES gyms(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  awarded_at timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, gym_id)
);

CREATE TABLE battles (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  player_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  opponent_type text NOT NULL CHECK (opponent_type IN ('wild','gym_leader','ai_trainer')),
  gym_id uuid REFERENCES gyms(id),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_progress' CHECK (status IN ('in_progress','completed','abandoned')),
  winner_id uuid REFERENCES users(id),
  started_at timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  ended_at timestamptz
);

CREATE TABLE battle_participants (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  battle_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES battles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  creature_instance_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES creature_instances(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  side text NOT NULL CHECK (side IN ('player','opponent')),
  starting_hp int NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE battle_turns (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  battle_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES battles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  turn_number int NOT NULL,
  actor_side text NOT NULL CHECK (actor_side IN ('player','opponent')),
  stat_category_chosen text NOT NULL CHECK (stat_category_chosen IN ('attack','defense','speed','special')),
  ability_triggered_id uuid REFERENCES abilities(id),
  damage_dealt int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  was_type_advantaged boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE battle_events (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  battle_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES battles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  event_type text NOT NULL CHECK (event_type IN ('strategic_swing','completion','abandonment')),

## What is Higgsfield MCP?

Higgsfield MCP connects Higgsfield's image, video, and audio models to the AI chat you already work in. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets an AI agent call external tools. Once Higgsfield is connected, the agent can draft a script, pick a model, run the generation, and return a finished file, all inside one conversation. Higgsfield is an AI-native creative suite, and MCP is how it plugs into your AI workflow.

Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop), Cursor, and CLI-based agents such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes connect through the Higgsfield MCP server. ChatGPT connects through the official Higgsfield plugin from the Plugins Directory. Both routes use the same account and the same credits.

The model catalog covers 30+ options, including Seedance, Kling, and Soul. The agent selects a model that fits the task, or you can name one yourself in the prompt.

Setup takes a few minutes: in Claude, add a custom connector with the Higgsfield MCP server URL; in ChatGPT, add the Higgsfield plugin. An active subscription is required. Step-by-step instructions for every agent are in the help center guide: How do I connect Higgsfield to Claude, ChatGPT, or another AI agent?

competitors.marketSummary: The launch/demo video space is rapidly being reshaped by Higgsfield's open MCP, which has spawned an ecosystem of official skills (UGC Factory, Faceless Content Factory) and a handful of small open-source projects (reeljet, Higgsfield Director MCP, AI Promo Video) that chain Higgsfield or code-based rendering (Revideo/FFmpeg) to automate promo videos for indie founders. Most solutions today are either generic ad/UGC generators requiring manual prompting, or developer-only open-source skills with no hosted UI, support, or business model. None combine deep codebase/context ingestion, a guided intake of founder instructions/preferences, and a fully hosted, non-technical SaaS experience purpose-built for startup launch videos.

hld.dataFlow: User signs up (Supabase Auth) → creates a Project via intake wizard, entering product description, tone/platform preferences, and uploading screenshots/screen-recordings/logo (stored in Supabase Storage, referenced in DB) → Context Extraction Service parses any supplied repo text/README into structured context, saved to `project_context` → Script Generation Service calls LLM with context to produce `script` + `shot_list` + captions, shown to user for review/edit → user approves; Higgsfield Orchestration Service computes estimated credit cost and displays for explicit approval → on approval, a `render_job` row is created and a job is enqueued → Job Worker submits the job to Higgsfield's API, polls/receives webhook updates, updates `render_job.status` → on completion, worker fetches 16:9 and 9:16 outputs, burns captions, generates thumbnail/publishing kit text, stores final files as `assets` linked to the job → Web App polls job status and displays finished video(s) for download/publish once `status = completed`; Stripe billing gates job creation to active-subscription users throughout.
hld.overview: ShipReel is a hosted Next.js SaaS that converts a founder's repo context, uploaded assets, and launch instructions into a finished multi-format launch video by orchestrating Higgsfield's video-generation API. Users go through a guided intake wizard (no MCP/CLI/prompt engineering), the backend extracts context (repo README/package.json or manual input), generates a script/shot-list via an LLM, assembles a Higgsfield render job with uploaded screenshots/screen-recordings, previews estimated credit cost for approval, submits the render, polls/receives webhook status, then produces 16:9 and 9:16 exports with burned-in captions and a publishing kit (title/description/hashtags/thumbnail). Billing is a flat-fee subscription abstracting raw Higgsfield credit costs.

engineering.schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  email text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  stripe_customer_id text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  stripe_subscription_id text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'trialing',
  plan text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'flat_69_monthly',
  current_period_end timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE projects (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  platform text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'product_hunt',
  tone text,
  product_description text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE project_context (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  readme_text text,
  package_json_text text,
  repo_url text,
  extracted_features jsonb DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE assets (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  render_job_id uuid,
  type text NOT NULL,
  storage_path text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE scripts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  script_text text NOT NULL,
  shot_list jsonb DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  captions jsonb DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE render_jobs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  script_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES scripts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  higgsfield_job_id text,
  estimated_credit_cost numeric,
  actual_credit_cost numeric,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending_approval',
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at timestamptz
);

ALTER TABLE assets ADD CONSTRAINT fk_assets_render_job FOREIGN KEY (render_job_id) REFERENCES render_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

CREATE TABLE publishing_kits (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  render_job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES render_jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title text,
  description text,
  hashtags jsonb DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

techStack.llm: OpenAI API (or equivalent LLM provider) for context extraction summarization, script/shot-list generation, and publishing-kit copy generation.
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth (email/password + optional GitHub OAuth for future repo-connect), JWT-based session, RLS enforced at the DB layer.
techStack.infra: Vercel for hosting/CI-CD of the Next.js app; Supabase Storage for asset/video file storage; Stripe for subscription billing; Higgsfield API/MCP as the core video-generation provider; Inngest or Trigger.dev for durable background job orchestration and webhook handling.
techStack.backend: Next.js Route Handlers (Node runtime) for API endpoints; background job worker implemented via a queue (Supabase Edge Functions or a lightweight worker service e.g. Inngest/Trigger.dev) for long-running Higgsfield render polling and post-processing.
techStack.database: Supabase Postgres with Row Level Security policies scoping all tables to the authenticated user_id (via project ownership).
techStack.devtools: TypeScript, ESLint/Prettier, Supabase CLI for local dev/migrations, GitHub Actions for CI (lint/build/test), Vercel preview deployments for PR review.
techStack.frontend: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS, deployed as a single full-stack app; guided multi-step wizard UI with client-side upload progress and job-status polling via SWR/React Query.

engineeringTasks.description: Wire up Supabase Auth (email/password) in Next.js, create protected route middleware, integrate Stripe Checkout/webhooks for flat-fee subscription creation, and enforce active-subscription checks before allowing render job creation.

engineeringTasks.title: Deploy pipeline setup
engineeringTasks.description: Connect repo to Vercel for automatic preview/production deployments, configure environment variables (Supabase keys, Stripe keys, Higgsfield API keys, LLM API keys), and set up GitHub Actions for lint/build checks on PRs.

engineeringTasks.title: Build guided intake wizard and asset upload flow
engineeringTasks.description: Create the multi-step form (product description, tone, platform, screenshots/screen-recordings/logo upload to Supabase Storage) that creates a Project, ProjectContext, and Asset records.

engineeringTasks.title: Build script/shot-list generation and review UI
engineeringTasks.description: Implement the LLM-backed endpoint that consumes ProjectContext to generate a Script (script_text, shot_list, captions), plus a review/edit UI where the founder approves or edits before render submission.

engineeringTasks.title: Build Higgsfield orchestration and cost-approval flow
engineeringTasks.description: Implement the service that builds a Higgsfield render request from the approved Script and Assets, computes estimated_credit_cost for user approval, submits the job, and creates a RenderJob record in pending_approval/queued state.

engineeringTasks.title: Build background worker for job polling and multi-format export
engineeringTasks.description: Implement a durable background job (Inngest/Trigger.dev or Supabase Edge Function cron) that polls/receives Higgsfield webhooks, updates RenderJob status, fetches 16:9 and 9:16 outputs plus burned-in captions, generates a thumbnail, stores results as Assets, and creates the PublishingKit.

engineeringTasks.title: Build job status dashboard and final video delivery UI
engineeringTasks.description: Create the project dashboard showing RenderJob status in real time, and once completed, display/download both video formats along with the generated PublishingKit (title, description, hashtags, thumbnail).

openEngineeringQuestions: What markup on Higgsfield API/credit costs is needed to sustain a $69/mo flat fee without eroding margin, and how should estimated_credit_cost be computed per job type?
Should GitHub repo OAuth be required at signup, or is screenshot-only ingestion sufficient for the 72-hour MVP, and does this change the ProjectContext schema now vs. later?

What minimum codebase signal (README, package.json, live URL) reliably produces accurate narrative extraction within the build window, and should this be validated with a fallback to manual-only input?

Do we proxy/store rendered videos ourselves in Supabase Storage or serve directly from Higgsfield's storage/CDN for v1, and what are the implications for asset retention, egress cost, and long-term URL stability?
How do we handle Higgsfield job failures/retries without double-charging credits, and what user-facing retry/refund policy should the render_jobs.status flow support?

What is the polling vs. webhook strategy for Higgsfield job status, and does the chosen background job framework (Inngest/Trigger.dev/Edge Functions) reliably support the expected render durations (minutes to tens of minutes)?
